Package com.csse3200.game.perks

Class PerkService

java.lang.Object
com.csse3200.game.perks.PerkService
public final class PerkService extends Object
Central registry and progress tracker for every Perk in the game. Any gameplay system - existing or future - reports progress toward a milestone with a single call:

PerkService.recordEvent("dashUsed", 1);

Adding a new perk tied to an EXISTING event key needs zero changes anywhere else - just a new entry in PerkDefinitions. Adding a perk for a brand-new milestone needs one new recordEvent(...) call at the point that milestone happens (e.g. inside the wall-jump code, once it exists), plus a new PerkDefinitions entry - nothing about this class changes either way.

Unlocked/progress/active state persists via Preferences, the same pattern PauseMenuDisplay already uses for audio settings - but only within one playthrough: it survives death/revive (that never touches this class at all), but resetAll() is called on every fresh game start (Start or Restart, not Load) - see MainGameScreen's constructor.

Unlocking a perk (permanent, once earned) is separate from making it active (up to 2 at a time, freely toggled via activate(java.lang.String)/deactivate(java.lang.String) - see the perk-selection screen shown after death). Only active perks' rewards actually apply - see e.g. ShieldComponent, which checks Perk.isActive() when a new player entity is created.

  • Method Details

    • register

      public static void register(Perk perk)
      Registers a perk definition and loads any previously-saved progress for it. Call once per perk (see PerkDefinitions.registerAll()) before any recordEvent(...) calls for it will have any effect. Safe to call again for the same id - re-registering just reloads saved state, it doesn't duplicate the perk.

    • recordEvent

      public static void recordEvent(String eventKey, int amount)
      Reports progress toward every registered perk listening for this event key. Safe to call for a key with no matching perks - it's simply a no-op, so gameplay code never needs to check whether a perk exists before calling this.

    • activate

      public static boolean activate(String id)
      Makes an unlocked perk active, if there's room. This is the only place a perk's active state is changed, so the 2-active rule only needs to live here.
      Parameters:
      id - the perk to activate
      Returns:
      true if it's now active - false if the id is unknown, the perk isn't unlocked yet, it was already active, or 2 perks are already active

    • deactivate

      public static void deactivate(String id)
      Makes a perk inactive. Safe to call on an already-inactive or unregistered id - a no-op either way.
      Parameters:
      id - the perk to deactivate

    • resetAll

      public static void resetAll()
      Clears every registered perk's progress/unlocked/active state, in memory and on disk. Called on every fresh game start (Start or Restart, not Load) - see MainGameScreen's constructor - and usable as a debug/testing hook too.

    • resetPerk

      public static void resetPerk(String id)
      Debug/testing hook - locks a single perk back to zero progress (and inactive), in memory and on disk. Safe to call for an unregistered id - it's simply a no-op.

      Note this only resets the perk's own tracked state. It does not revert any gameplay reward already applied to a live entity this session (e.g. a shield's extended duration) - that reward was applied directly to that component's state when the perk was active at entity creation, so a fresh player entity (e.g. after a respawn) is needed to see the change reflected.

      Parameters:
      id - the perk's id, as passed to its Perk constructor
